newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-BIG THREE CHALLENGE LOCAL TRIO.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BIG THREE CHALLENGE LOCAL TRIO.

text.p: New Zealander Michael Long and Australians Anthony Painter and Peter Lonard shared a two-shot lead after the third round in the European PGA Tour opener on Saturday.

But the local trio will be looking over their shoulders in Sunday's final round after three of the top six players in the world rankings -- Ernie Els, Nick Faldo and Fred Couples -- moved into contention.
Long, Painter and Lonard ended the third day at the 700,000 sterling (US$1.1 million) Johnnie Walker Classic at nine under par for a total 207 on the par-72, Hope Island resort course.
South African Els shot a one-under par 71 on Saturday to move to seven under, two shots ahead of American Fred Couples, who equalled the course record with a round of 67 in blustery conditions.
Englishman Faldo, who lurked a further shot back at four under, said he could enjoy an advantage coming from behind on the final day if the wind blows again at its strongest in the afternoon.
"To go out earlier, before the wind gets up, and post a target would be the best way to do it," Faldo told reporters after his third round 70.
"In this wind, a 67 is a very good score. If I can make that on Sunday I would be right there at the finish, for sure," the U.S. Masters champion said.
Although exasperated by his putting, Faldo was pleased with the rest of his game so early in the season, saying: "The swing is going well, especially in this wind..."
Couples adopted more aggressive tactics to drag himself back up the leaderboard after Friday's four-over par 76, which included a triple bogey eight on the par five ninth.
"I needed to hit the driver on every hole to make the course short," Couples said. "It worked most of the time. I dodged most of the pot bunkers and had short shots to the green."
Long, the overnight leader at eight under, held a three-shot lead early in his round before three bogeys in four holes on the back nine brought him back into the field.
Lonard, meanwhile, fired his third successive 69, while Painter equalled the course record 67 to take a share of the lead.

Both Lonard and Painter said they would seriously consider playing the rest of the season in Europe if they gained an exemption by winning the tournament, which is jointly sanctioned by the Australian PGA Tour.
Asked about his thoughts on three players from the local tour leading the tournament, Painter joked: "We've brought all these other guys over to Australia just to show we are better than them."
